Count fragments in fixed-width genome tiles

Source: R/RunGenomeTiles.R
RunGenomeTiles.Rd

Construct explicit non-overlapping genome tiles and delegate validated sparse fragment counting to RecountATAC(). No peaks are needed for defining the tile universe; the source ChromatinAssay supplies verified fragment mappings and reference provenance.

Usage

RunGenomeTiles(
  object,
  assay = NULL,
  seqlengths = NULL,
  chromosomes = NULL,
  bin.size = 5000L,
  cells = NULL,
  new.assay = NULL,
  process_n = 2000L,
  max.tiles = 2000000L,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

object

A Seurat object with a validated ChromatinAssay and fragments.

assay

Source chromatin assay; NULL uses the active assay.

seqlengths

Optional named positive integer chromosome lengths. NULL uses declared assay lengths, which must all be known for selected contigs. Supplied lengths must agree with known assay lengths. Names are not used to guess assembly or chromosome style.

chromosomes

Optional unique contig names in desired output order.

bin.size

Positive integer tile width. The last tile per chromosome is truncated at that chromosome's end, never dropped or extended.

cells

Selected source-assay cells; see RecountATAC().

new.assay

Optional unused assay name; NULL returns counts/ranges/receipt.

process_n

FeatureMatrix chunk size; see RecountATAC().

max.tiles

Positive integer upper bound on tile count before allocation.

verbose

Whether to print progress messages.

Value

The RecountATAC() return value with tile parameters in its receipt. Counts are overlapping fragment records, not insertion endpoints or unique fragments across bins. A fragment crossing a boundary can count in two bins.

See also

RecountATAC()
